<!-- pr-reviewer: bc5e9b00823a6a8d34c07bb7fb52a09bbad540e5 -->
**Needs changes before merge.** NeoTech's two items from the 81adfa35 review are fixed at this head. One new blocker: the `step` measurement rounds the move in world coordinates, not in the origin-relative coordinates the post writes. With a non-zero work offset in an inch program, a capped feed can still drive A far past its stated rate. There is also one small rounding gap in the uncapped branch.

Safety tier: this PR changes posted G-code feeds. Hub (Tormach only) cannot exercise fanuc.cps, doosan-dnm.cps or fanuc-lathe.cps, so no Hub run is requested. The checks below are local and headless.

### What looks good
- **Item 1 (inch capped F): addressed.** `rotaryFeedWord` (`crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs`) floors in the post's unit: 0.1 mm/min, or 0.001 in/min in inch. It floors after converting mm/min to in/min, so the inch word is never above the cap. The "under 0.1 mm/min" refusal is judged in mm before converting. Mutation checks: `ceil` or `round` in place of the inch floor fails `an_inch_program_posts_the_capped_feed_in_inch`. Judging the refusal in inch fails `the_slow_feed_refusal_is_judged_in_mm_in_both_units`.
- **Item 2 (any of A, B, C): addressed.** Both TCP paths pass `["A","B","C"]` to `rotaryFeed`. Cutting fanuc.cps or doosan-dnm.cps (TCP) back to `["A"]` fails `a_feed_turning_c_alone_holds_the_stated_c_rate`. One note: the `!has(p.A) && !has(p.B) && !has(p.C)` gate in `feedWord` is not pinned (reverting it to A only passes all 9 tests). That is because both dialects' `tilt()` returns `[]` and writes no rotary word when the record has no A. So the gate is unreachable today, and the letters list is what enforces the item.
- **`step`: does what it claims.** Removing the step argument from both posts lets an inch move run A over the rate, and the pin catches it: `A at 1007.7 deg/min past 1000: G01 X0.3976 Y0 Z0 A30 F0.131` (`an_inch_program_posts_the_capped_feed_in_inch`, fanuc and doosan each on their own).
- **NeoTech's merged test (bound widened 0.1%).** That bound compares the inch F with the mm F. It does not check against the machine rate. The rate check is `assert_within_in`. I tightened its tolerance locally from `* 1.0005` to exact (`1 + 1e-12`) and all 9 tests still pass. So no capped block in these streams posts over the stated A rate or the linear limit, and the widened comparison bound does not hide an over-rate post.
- The fanuc-lathe change is a faithful refactor: the same `lcmd`, the same `fmax` guard on `lin > EPS`, the same C cap. `c_axis_unwind` and `c_axis_live` pass, and their goldens are unchanged.
- `fourth_axis_pose::tilted()` gains a placing rapid. The fixture change is explained and its assertions are unchanged. No goldens or snapshots change, `CHANGELOG.md` is untouched, and no process files are touched. The new module has its provenance line. Body has `Changelog:` and `Fixes #885`.

### Local results (head bc5e9b00 merged with upstream/main 08ea337e, clean merge, macOS debug)
| Suite | Result |
|---|---|
| camcraft-post lib | 44 passed |
| post `script_fanuc` / `script_doosan_dnm` / `script_fanuc_lathe` | 11 / 11 / 15 passed |
| post `fanuc_post` / `doosan_dnm_post` / `post_engine` | 12 / 9 / 33 passed |
| app `rotary_feed_cap` | 9 passed |
| app `conformance` / `golden_cl` | 7 / 32 passed |
| app `program_units` / `post_unit_word` | 7 / 5 passed |
| app `fourth_axis_pose` / `c_axis_unwind` / `c_axis_live` / `tormach_fourth_axis` / `posting` / `machine_library` | 9 / 7 / 5 / 12 / 17 / 11 passed |
| `cargo clippy -p camcraft-post -p camcraft-app --all-targets -- -D warnings` | clean |

### Requested before merge
1. **Blocker: the posted length is measured without the work offset.** `crates/post/src/post/rotary_cap.rs:112` rounds `p.X` / `p.StartX` (world coordinates) to the step. The posts write `fu(v - orgX)` (`wo`, fanuc.cps:107, doosan-dnm.cps:131). When the origin is not on the output grid, the rounded world length and the posted length can differ by one step. That is the normal case in inch, since a metric origin is almost never a multiple of 0.0001 in. If the cap sees 0 while the block posts one step, the cap takes the "tip still" reading (F = rate). The control then reads that F as tip speed over 0.0001 in under G43.4.

   Reproduced on both posts (TCP trunnion, A rated 1000 deg/min, inch, move X10.000 -> X10.001 mm with A 0 -> 30):
   ```
   no origin:          G01 X0.3937 Y0 Z0 A30 F39.37   (tip still: OK)
   PARAM OriginX 1:    G01 X0.3544 Y0 Z0 A30 F39.37   (0.0001 in of tip at 39.37 in/min -> A about 11,800,000 deg/min)
   ```
   Fix: quantize the origin-relative coordinates, the ones the block actually posts. For example, pass the origin (`[orgX, orgY, orgZ]`) to `rotaryFeed`, or have `feedWord` hand it `X - orgX` and the other two axes. Pin it with an inch program carrying `PARAM OriginX 1` and this one-thou move, asserted through `assert_within_in`.
2. **Small: an uncapped F can post over the cap after `ff()` rounds it.** `feedWord` decides "capped" from the unrounded F (`rotaryFeed` returns `capped: g < f - 1e-9`). Then `if (!r.capped) return fw(p.FeedRate)` (fanuc.cps:640, doosan-dnm.cps:767) rounds to a whole mm/min, or 0.01 in/min in inch. That can land above the cap.

   Reproduced in mm (A rated 1000): an op F of 999.6 over 2.999 mm with 3 deg of A posts `A3 F1000`, so A runs at 1000.33 deg/min (+0.03%). An op F of 9.6 over 0.029 mm with 3 deg posts `A6 F10`, so A runs at 1034 deg/min (+3.4%). The overshoot is at most 0.5 mm/min (0.005 in/min) of F. So it is negligible at normal feeds but not bounded relative to the rate at slow ones. The control's own per-axis feed clamp would limit the axis, but the post's promise ("never past the stated rate") does not hold.

   Fix: when the turn has a stated rate, judge the posted word, not `f`. If `ff(f)`, read back in mm/min, is above `g`, post `rotaryFeedWord(g, inch)`. Pin it with the 999.6-over-2.999 move.

### Questions / notes (not blocking)
- fanuc-lathe.cps's `fm()` (`toFixed(1)`, rounding, not flooring) has the same pre-existing round-up, up to 0.05 mm/min over the C cap. It predates this PR; a follow-up issue is enough.
- `assert_within` / `assert_within_in` allow 0.05% over (`* 1.0005`, rotary_feed_cap.rs:112-113). The capped blocks hold exactly, so the tolerance could be dropped, which would make the pin strictly "never over".
- In inch, a capped pure-rotary block (tip still) posts the mm/min cap converted to in/min, e.g. `A30 F39.37`. If the control reads F on a rotary-only block as deg/min, A turns 25.4x slower than the stated rate. Likewise, the composite (no TCP) cap in inch is conservative by up to 25.4x, because the control then counts degrees against inches. Both are safe and only cost time; worth a line in the decision file.
- The `!has(p.A) && !has(p.B) && !has(p.C)` gate is unreachable today, as noted above. That is fine as defence in depth, but it is not what the C test pins.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
